attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No Yang-Mills estimate yet supplies H,K,L with a uniform collar remainder for reflected Wilson hairpin products in the locked algebra.
steps: Start with the exact finite same-theory criterion q_eta=\widehat N_eta\oslash\widehat B_eta>=0 for each locked Wilson block after additive contacts are removed.
Normalize the common boundary footprint so q_eta tends to J=11^*=nee^* as the collar collapses.
Decompose the matrix into the vacuum direction e and P=I-ee^*. Since e^*q_eta e=n+O(eta)>0, apply the Schur complement.
Expand the Schur complement R_eta. The eta^2 coefficient is not PKP alone; the rank-one vacuum direction subtracts n^{-1}PHee^*HP, recovering the cycle-226 correction.
Keep one more order. The eta^3 coefficient acquires two mixed vacuum terms and one scalar inverse term: C=PLP-n^{-1}(PHee^*KP+PKee^*HP)+n^{-2}(e^*He)PHee^*HP.

Now reduce R_eta first by the positive range of A=PHP. If A has kernel Pi, positivity forces Pi B Pi>=0. If Pi B Pi has null space Omega, the next necessary test is Omega(Pi C Pi-Pi B A^dagger B Pi)Omega>=0.
This shows cycle 226 was the correct second-order gate but not the final null-direction gate; a third-order Wilson boundary OPE can be the first valid falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-dimensional tangent cone is valid, but the actual continuum construction must still prove the boundary OPE expansion and identify q_eta with the same-theory Schur-preimage rather than a boundary-renormalized variant.

assumptions: For every eta>0 before collapse the regulated/collar OS matrix is positive and the Schur-preimage q_eta is the intended same-theory target matrix.
q_eta is Hermitian and admits a uniform expansion q_eta=J+eta H+eta^2 K+eta^3 L+o(eta^3) on the finite block.
The vacuum block e^*q_eta e remains positive for small eta.
A=PHP has closed range in the finite-dimensional block; A^dagger is its Moore-Penrose inverse on P-space.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive collar Wilson/local Schwinger matrices N_eta together with boundary anomaly matrices B_eta for a fixed locked gauge-invariant finite family.
target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions on the same locked gauge-invariant Wilson/local test algebra.
controlled interface: normalized Schur-preimage q_eta=\widehat N_eta\oslash\widehat B_eta, projected off the vacuum vector e=n^{-1/2}(1,...,1).

same-theory condition: collar collapse identifies the same renormalized Wilson/local observables; diagonal congruences already in the locked normalization are allowed, but no boundary counterterm, quotient algebra change, or extra boundary state is allowed.
J=11^*=n ee^*, P=I-ee^*, eta is the collar scale or first valid asymptotic scale.

equations.label: Schur-preimage interface
equations.valid_when: The boundary anomaly is multiplicative on the finite Wilson block after additive positive contacts have been eliminated and diagonal normalizations are locked.

equations.label: vacuum Feshbach reduction
equations.valid_when: e^*q_eta e>0; then q_eta>=0 is equivalent to R_eta>=0 by the Schur complement.

equations.label: first three reduced coefficients
equations.valid_when: The expansion of q_eta is uniform through order eta^3.

equations.label: coefficients
equations.valid_when: J=nee^* is the rank-one vacuum matrix and e is unit normalized.

equations.label: third coefficient
equations.valid_when: H,K,L are Hermitian coefficient matrices in q_eta=J+eta H+eta^2K+eta^3L+o(eta^3).

equations.label: third-order null test
equations.valid_when: A>=0, Pi projects onto ker A, Pi B Pi>=0, and Omega projects onto ker(Pi B Pi).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find z in ker(Pi B Pi) with z^*(Pi C Pi-Pi B A^dagger B Pi)z<0; this is a valid same-theory OS falsifier even when the first- and second-order tests pass.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Sharpens the Wilson boundary obstruction beyond the second-order test by adding the missing Feshbach correction from the positive first-order sector.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Third-order tangent-cone bridge for locked Wilson collar quotients. For a finite Wilson hairpin block with normalized Schur-preimage q_eta=J+eta H+eta^2 K+eta^3 L+o(eta^3), OS positivity of the intended same-theory matrix forces a vacuum Feshbach hierarchy: A>=0 on 1^perp, then the corrected B is >=0 on ker A, then the corrected C-B A^dagger B is >=0 on the null of that B. Any negative form at the first failing level is a finite Wilson falsifier.

assumptions: PHP>=mu P on 1^perp for some mu>0.
The vacuum block e^*q_eta e=n+O(eta) is positive.
definitions: finite block: a fixed list of locked reflected Wilson collar observables with common normalized boundary footprint.

equations.label: finite-block lower bound
equations.valid_when: eta is small compared with mu divided by the uniform O(eta^2) norm bound.

equations.label: block positivity
equations.valid_when: The Schur complement is taken with respect to the vacuum direction e.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If PHP has a negative eigenvalue, positivity fails at order eta; if it has null vectors, the branch must use the second- and third-order tests instead.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Gives a promotion test: a positive first-order boundary kernel on the reduced Wilson block proves local collar-collapse OS positivity without computing K,L.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Positive-gap simplification. If the first reduced boundary OPE coefficient A=PHP is strictly positive on 1^perp, then all sufficiently small higher-order mixed Wilson boundary terms are harmless for this finite block: q_eta is positive for small eta.

assumptions: Diagonal Wilson factors are already included in the same-theory normalization.
Coefficient changes induced by changing only individual Wilson normalizations are infinitesimal diagonal congruences of J.
The finite block is normalized to unit diagonal before forming q_eta.
definitions: one-body anomaly: coefficient matrices of the form u1^*+1u^* and their higher-order diagonal-congruence descendants.
mixed anomaly: any coefficient not representable by a locked diagonal congruence.
reduced test space: 1^perp and successive null spaces produced by the Feshbach hierarchy.

equations.label: one-body cancellation
equations.valid_when: P projects onto 1^perp and u is any finite vector.

equations.label: congruence invariance
equations.valid_when: D_eta is a diagonal normalization already locked into the same continuum theory.

equations.label: reduced obstruction survives
equations.valid_when: x,y,z lie in the respective reduced/null spaces; these forms discard pure one-body factors.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed obstruction disappears after imposing unit diagonal and projecting to 1^perp, it was only a one-body normalization, not a same-theory failure.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents false positives: a negative reduced form is a genuine mixed boundary falsifier, not a removable Wilson normalization artifact.
candidate_lemmas.statement: One-body Wilson renormalizations remain invisible to the reduced tangent tests through third order; only mixed boundary OPE coefficients can survive the P/Feshbach hierarchy.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot only if reflected Wilson collar products lack a valid common-footprint asymptotic expansion or the locked algebra cannot realize finite blocks testing the reduced forms.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the RG/OPE machinery proves uniform H,K,L expansions and nonnegativity of the Feshbach hierarchy on a dense locked Wilson core.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a sharper finite-dimensional bridge with a new third-order correction and concrete Yang-Mills coefficient targets H,K,L.

dependency_updates.description: The closed-cone passage remains formal on fixed collars; the nonformal bridge now includes a finite Feshbach tangent hierarchy for Wilson boundary collapse.
The locked algebra must contain enough reflected Wilson hairpin blocks to test H,K,L and their reduced null forms; otherwise a boundary anomaly may be invisible to the realized cone.
The topology must control finite reflected OS matrices through the collar scale with uniform o(eta^3) remainders, not merely pointwise Schwinger distribution convergence.

falsifiers: First-order falsifier: there exists x in 1^perp with x^*PHPx<0 for a realized reflected Wilson block.
Second-order falsifier: PHP>=0 but some y in ker(PHP) has y^*(PKP-n^{-1}PHee^*HP)y<0.
Third-order falsifier: the first two gates pass but some z in ker(Pi B Pi) has z^*(Pi C Pi-Pi B A^dagger B Pi)z<0.
Topology falsifier: RG convergence is too weak to produce a valid uniform expansion for q_eta on reflected Wilson collar products.
Same-theory falsifier: the expansion becomes positive only after adding a boundary counterterm or changing Wilson-loop renormalization at the reflection plane.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 227 adds the next valid obstruction after the second-order correction. Once the vacuum rank-one direction is removed, null directions of PHP require a genuine Feshbach hierarchy: the third-order test contains -Pi B A^dagger B Pi from coupling to the positive first-order sector. Thus PKP and PLP alone are not reliable Wilson falsifier tests. A positive first-order reduced kernel promotes a finite block immediately, while any negative reduced coefficient at the first nonzero Feshbach level is a normalization-safe mixed boundary falsifier.
